public_rationale: The official hearing record establishes Altman's affirmative support for licensing and government oversight alongside Marcus. Documentary reporting establishes that OpenAI privately advocated narrower EU obligations. These support both factual components. They do not establish hypocrisy: supporting regulation generally is compatible with contesting particular provisions.
limitations: The lobbying finding relies on reputable reporting because the available primary PDF extraction is corrupted.
The evidence does not establish that OpenAI alone caused any legislative change.
The documented lobbying includes activity before the Senate hearing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Sam Altman told the Senate, standing next to Marcus, that he strongly favored AI regulation, but behind the scenes his team fought to water down the EU AI Act.
conditions: behind the scenes, by his team

statement.excerpt: When Sam Altman stood next to me in the Senate, he told the Senate that he strongly favored AI regulation. But behind the scenes his team fought to water down the EU AI Act.
statement.document_title: Why California’s AI Safety Bill should (still) be signed into law - and why that won’t be nearly enough

from_speaker: stood next to me in the Senate
behind the scenes his team fought to water down the EU AI Act
our_interpretation: Standing next to Marcus means appearing alongside him at the same Senate hearing, not a claim about their physical posture.
Strongly favored regulation means an affirmative endorsement of government rules or oversight.
Water down means seeking narrower coverage or fewer obligations in the proposed EU law. It does not imply opposition to every form of regulation.
The historical comparison encompasses OpenAI's 2022 EU engagement and the May 16, 2023 hearing; it does not require the lobbying to have followed the hearing.
criteria.support_condition: The hearing record establishes Altman's endorsement alongside Marcus, and documentary evidence establishes OpenAI personnel privately advocating reduced obligations under the EU proposal.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The hearing record contradicts the endorsement or joint appearance, or reliable records establish that the alleged lobbying instead sought equivalent or stronger obligations without the claimed narrowing.

evidence.locator: Senator Graham's exchange about an agency overseeing AI developers, immediately followed by his question to Marcus
evidence.publisher: U.S. Senate Committee on the Judiciary / Government Publishing Office
evidence.explanation: Altman enthusiastically endorsed a proposed oversight agency and also endorsed licensing. The same exchange includes Marcus, establishing their participation in the hearing.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following the announcement that TIME is publishing OpenAI's white paper; related September 2022 submission discussion
evidence.explanation: The report describes OpenAI's submission seeking exemptions and removal of provisions that would classify its general-purpose systems as high risk. It also reports the company's explanation that it was responding to policymakers and continued to support safe AI regulation.
